newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US bond vols edge up, puts purchased.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US bond vols edge up, puts purchased.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond implied volatilities rose Wednesday as the underlying futures skidded, and floor traders said interest in buying put options also picked up.
"There appeared to be new put buying. People are hedging to the downside at least," said a bond options broker for a U.S. banking firm.

Futures staged an abrupt selloff at midday on talk that hedge funds were continuing to unwind so-called yen-carry trades due to the dollar's recent steep drop and on disappointment at futures' failure to make further headway to the upside after repeated probes above 110-00.
The June bond contract settled 18/32 lower at 109-09.
The afternoon slide in prices pushed up volatilities, which had been drifting lower in the morning as futures meandered, floor traders said.
"It is the first time that volatility has picked up in a while," said the options broker. "People who are expecting a rough ride down pumped it up."

Interest rate volatility levels slid Tuesday in typical post-event fashion after the Federal Reserve announced it had decided to leave U.S. short-term rates unchanged. They finished the day at 7.75 percent for July options and 8.14 percent for September.
Volatilities opened about 0.1 point higher this morning, slipped, then bounced back late to end the day at 7.90 percent in July and 8.25 percent in September.

Trading in options was hectic as market participants looked to hedge their downside price exposure, floor brokers said. Among the larger transactions, a European bank bought an estimated 4,000 September 106-00 puts.

Earlier in the session, a U.S. banking firm bought 2,000 September 112-00/114-00 call spreads against June bond futures when they were trading at 109-29, and a dealer firm bought 1,000 July 111-00 calls. Later, another bank sold 2,000 July 112 calls around futures' closing price.
Eurodollar options traders also noticed an increase in put purchases.
One large dealer firm was seen buying 2,000 March 93.25 puts. Several large-size sales of short-dated June 93.50 straddles also went through.
Volatilities mostly declined in the short end, where prices did not follow the selloff in Treasurys. September volatility slipped to 8.8 percent and December to 10.6 percent.
December Eurodollar futures ended unchanged at at 93.735.
